Update:: well I finally won my money back by reminding walking yoga of the law and their responsibilities under the law regarding “auto-renewals”, so if anyone who wanted to cancel but didn’t get the renewals notification from the company need to be aware of their rights under the law. The law is there to protect the consumers not these app’s. 

 Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, apps must send timely reminders before auto-renewals to inform customers of upcoming charges, price increases, and how to cancel, aiming to prevent "subscription traps". While some platforms like Apple provide reminders, the obligation now falls on businesses, requiring clear communication, simple cancellation paths, and transparency about renewal terms to comply with evolving consumer protection laws. 
Key Legal Requirements (UK Focus)
Timely Reminder: A notice must be sent a reasonable time before the auto-renewal date.
Clear Information: The reminder must state the renewal date, amount due, details of any price increases, and clear instructions on how to cancel.
Easy Cancellation: Consumers must be able to cancel as easily as they signed up, with accessible cancellation routes. 
Best Practices & Platform Rules
Before Signing Up: Clear information about auto-renewal and cancellation must be presented upfront.
Platform-Specifics: Apple and Google have their own rules, but the DMCC Act adds broader legal obligations for developers.
Proactive Developers: Many apps already send reminders, often via email or in-app notifications, to build trust and avoid issues. 
What to Do if You Don't Get a Reminder
Contact the Company: Reach out to the app or service provider as soon as you notice the charge, as many will offer refunds for unexpected renewals.
Check Platform Settings: Look for active subscriptions in your Apple ID or Google Play settings, though some website-based subscriptions won't appear there.
